Architecture ticket. We have a brownfield estate whose vCenter, ESXi/vSAN, NSX, Live Site Recovery, and vSphere Replication were installed and patched as separately managed point solutions. Bring it under one VMware Cloud Foundation fleet. The exact estate is in `inventory/estate.json`; the requested destination is VCF 9.1.0.0. Several installed builds are chronologically newer than the corresponding 9.1.0.0 bundle builds, so treating a larger marketing version as an ordinary in-place upgrade would be a back-in-time regression. Produce an executable architecture, not an explanatory report.

Research before implementation using genuine network access. Consult Broadcom's currently published compatibility/interoperability and upgrade-path material for the component combinations in the inventory, including the VCF 9.1 guidance relevant to back-in-time builds and the Live Site Recovery/vSphere Replication transition. Choose the Broadcom sources and searches yourself. Record every source actually consulted in `research/consulted-sources.json` with a UTC ISO-8601 `researchedAt` value ending in `Z` and a nonempty `sources` array; each entry must contain nonempty string fields `url`, `title`, and `claimsUsed`, with a real reachable HTTP(S) URL and the claims used from that source. In your final response cite those same sources and call out any disagreement between the live material and the pinned snapshot. The local `compatibility/vcf-9.1.0.0-snapshot.json` is the stable implementation authority for this exercise even if the live pages have changed. Do not replace live research with that snapshot.

Implement a standard-library-only Python package named `vcf_arch`. Running

`python3 -m vcf_arch --inventory inventory/estate.json --compatibility compatibility/vcf-9.1.0.0-snapshot.json --output migration-plan.json`

must deterministically generate and retain `migration-plan.json`. The artifact is both the target VCF installer architecture and the ordered brownfield migration plan: its root must be an `SddcSpec` accepted by the bundled `specifications/vcf-installer/vcf-installer-openapi.json`, which is the Apache-2.0 specification from tag `9.1.0.0` of `vmware/vcf-api-specs`, and it must also conform to `schemas/migration-plan.schema.json`. Preserve every inventory component exactly once in `components`, including its installed version/build, pinned target, migration mode, and all technical gates that govern it. `steps` must be strictly ordered, dependency-consistent, name every estate component, avoid every prohibited direct transition in the snapshot, use replacement rather than downgrade for back-in-time components, transition the two legacy recovery appliances to the unified target named by the snapshot, and finish with all target components managed by the single fleet. Do not edit the inventory, pinned snapshot, schemas, installer specification, license, or verifier.

Run `python3 verify.py` as the acceptance check.
